You are given a k-Minimum Spanning Tree problem (k-MST).

Problem description:
- The input describes a connected, weighted, undirected graph.
- The input also specifies a target number of distinct nodes that the tree must span.

Decision:
- Choose a set of undirected edges from the input graph.

Feasibility constraints:
- The chosen edges must form a connected, cycle-free subgraph (a tree).
- The tree must span exactly the required number of DISTINCT nodes.
- Every chosen edge must appear in the input (same endpoints).

Objective:
- Minimize the total weight (sum of edge weights) of the chosen edges.

You will receive the instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Reply using exactly the following JSON structure (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": [[u1, v1], [u2, v2], ...]
}
```
Notes:
- Each [u, v] denotes an undirected edge. Use the exact node identifiers from the input.
- Ensure the solution is a tree and spans exactly the required number of nodes.
- Do not include explanations.

item_fields.description: the other endpoint node of an edge

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.description: weight/cost of the edge between u and v

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct city blocks in the neighborhood planning instance — i.e., the number of block identifiers available to choose from when selecting which blocks to include in the new connected cluster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate new streets (possible connections) between pairs of blocks that the planning team may choose to build; each is a potential edge in the k‑block road network.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of city blocks the planner must include in the resulting tree: the chosen blocks must form a single connected, loop‑free network and this number must equal k exactly.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint block identifier for a candidate street: the first city block that this potential new road would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint block identifier for the same candidate street: the second city block that this potential new road would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to construct that candidate street between the two blocks (u and v). These costs are the edge weights that are summed when evaluating the total construction expense of a chosen k‑block tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of servers (nodes) in the data-center network graph — the count of racks/servers available to choose from when building the cluster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible direct cable links (edges) between servers in the graph — the number of candidate straight connections with measured lengths.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of servers (k) that must be selected and wired into a single connected, loop-free cluster — the required size of the tree you must construct.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint server/rack for this potential direct link (one end of the cable). Use this ID to refer to which rack the link connects from.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint server/rack for this potential direct link (the other end of the cable).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or cost of the straight cable required to connect server_u and server_v; this is the value summed across chosen links to evaluate total cable used.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct campsites listed for this planning instance — each corresponds to a graph node and is a possible campsite you may select.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate trail segments provided between campsites — each entry is a possible path (edge) connecting two campsites that can be used when laying out the network.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of campsites you must select and connect into a single, loop-free network (a tree). Your chosen network must include exactly this many distinct campsites.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one endpoint campsite for this candidate trail segment. Matches one of the campsite identifiers from the global list.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other endpoint campsite for this candidate trail segment. Together with 'u' it defines which two campsites the trail would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (or cost) of the trail between the two endpoint campsites u and v. This positive number is what you sum across chosen trails to compare plans (minimize habitat disturbance).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct exhibit locations (nodes) available in the museum layout options. These are all the exhibits you may choose from when picking exactly k displays to connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible walkways (edges) listed between exhibits. Each represents a candidate path you could build between two exhibits, with a given length.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of exhibits that must be chosen and connected. Your final design must include exactly this many exhibits and connect them with walkways forming a tree (connected, no cycles).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a candidate walkway: the identifier (index or label) of the first exhibit that this walkway would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a candidate walkway: the identifier (index or label) of the second exhibit that this walkway would connect. The walkway is undirected — it connects u and v both ways.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The physical length (cost) of the candidate walkway between the two named exhibits. When evaluating layouts, you sum the lengths of chosen walkways and seek the minimum total for a connected acyclic selection spanning exactly k exhibits.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of towers in the region (the number of nodes available to choose from). This is the size of the pool of candidate towers the planner may select from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate point-to-point links (edges) between towers. Each represents a possible direct connection the planner can build, with an associated cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of towers the planner must select and interconnect. The chosen towers must form one connected, acyclic network (a tree) and this value fixes how many nodes the tree must span.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint tower of a candidate link. Combined with 'tower_endpoint_b' this specifies which two towers that link would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint tower of a candidate link. Together with 'tower_endpoint_a' it defines the pair of towers that the candidate link would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary or resource cost to establish the point-to-point link between the two specified towers. Planners sum these costs for chosen links and seek the selection with minimal total cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential supply locations (depots or crossroads) in the affected region — i.e., the number of graph nodes from which you may select depots.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available roads (possible connections) between locations in the region — i.e., the number of edges in the graph.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The predetermined number of supply depots that must be selected and connected into one loop-free network (the tree must span exactly this many locations).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location identifier for a given road (one of the two locations that this road connects). Use this together with 'location_v' to identify the road's endpoints.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location identifier for the same road (the second of the two locations that this road connects).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance (or cost) along the road that connects the two locations; distances are summed over chosen roads to compute total driving distance for the selected depot network.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of substations in the full electrical network instance (counting every node available to choose from, including those that may not be selected in the final k-substation plan).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential power line segments (edges) given in the instance — each is a possible cable route between two substations that could be built.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of substations that must be selected and connected into a single acyclic network (the tree must span exactly this many substations).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint substation for a potential power line segment; used with 'v' to define a candidate cable between two substations.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint substation for a potential power line segment; used with 'u' to define a candidate cable between two substations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Total cost of building the power line between the two endpoint substations (includes cable length and installation cost). These weights sum to give the plan's total cost when edges are chosen.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct warehouses listed in the data. This is the count of candidate warehouse locations (graph nodes) from which you may select exactly k to include in the shuttle network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential shuttle routes recorded between warehouses. Each entry corresponds to one undirected route (edge) with an associated measured distance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of warehouses the operations team must pick and connect. The final shuttle plan must span precisely this many warehouses (nodes) and contain no loops.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of one endpoint warehouse for this potential shuttle route. Matches one of the warehouses counted in total_warehouses_available.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of the other endpoint warehouse for this potential shuttle route. Together with warehouse_endpoint_a it defines the two warehouses this route would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Measured distance (or travel cost) of the shuttle route between the two warehouses listed in warehouse_endpoint_a and warehouse_endpoint_b. These distances are summed when evaluating a candidate network and should be minimized; routes are considered undirected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct scenic viewpoints available in the area (i.e., the number of candidate locations the crew can choose from).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct potential connectors (planned trails or bridges) considered between viewpoints; each represents a possible installation the crew could build.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of viewpoints the organizer must include in the final connected, acyclic trail system (the tree must span precisely this many viewpoints).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint viewpoint of a potential connector (one of the two scenic spots the connector would join).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint viewpoint of the same potential connector (the second scenic spot the connector would join).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The installation length (cost) of that potential connector (trail or bridge) between viewpoint_u and viewpoint_v; the objective sums these lengths for chosen connectors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct docks (harbor locations) shown on the map. These are the unique dock identifiers from which you may choose exactly k to include in the ferry plan.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of direct ferry route options available in the map. Each option is a possible direct leg between two docks with a known sailing distance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of docks the plan must include. The selected docks must be connected by direct legs into a tree (no closed loops), and the sum of the chosen legs' distances is to be minimized.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint dock for this direct ferry route option.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint dock for this route option. Together with 'dock_u' this specifies the two distinct docks that the leg would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Sailing distance (edge weight) for the direct ferry leg between 'dock_u' and 'dock_v'. These distances are added for chosen legs to compute the plan's total sailing distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct habitat patches available in the landscape that can be selected as part of the corridor network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of potential wildlife corridors (pairwise connections) measured between habitat patches that could be built to connect selected patches.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of habitat patches the planner must include in the final connected corridor network (the tree must span exactly this many patches).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint habitat patch for this candidate corridor (one of the two patches the corridor would connect).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint habitat patch for this candidate corridor (the second patch the corridor would connect).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The measured length (cost) of the candidate corridor connecting the two patches; this contributes to the total corridor length to be minimized when selecting the tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vendor booths/areas available at the festival. Each node represents a booth that could be chosen to receive service.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential direct service lines (possible pairwise connections) between booths listed in the instance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: Exact number of booths the coordinator must select and connect. The chosen booths must form a single connected, acyclic network (a tree) containing exactly this many booths.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one endpoint booth for this potential service line.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other endpoint booth for this potential service line.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or installation cost of the service line connecting booth_u and booth_v (e.g., meters of cable). The solver will sum these values for the chosen edges to compare layouts.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate bus stops (nodes) shown on the district map — i.e., all intersections or stop locations that could be included in the sidewalk network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential sidewalk links (edges) drawn between stops on the map — each is a possible sidewalk segment that could be built to connect two stops.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of bus stops that must be included in the final pedestrian network (the planner must choose exactly this many stops to connect with sidewalks).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint stop of a candidate sidewalk segment — identify which stop (by its node index or label) this segment connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint stop of the same candidate sidewalk segment — identify the stop at the other end of this segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of that candidate sidewalk segment between stop_u and stop_v; this is the amount added to the total sidewalk length if this segment is chosen.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of excavation sites on the map — every site that could possibly be chosen by the dig director.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate access tracks in the input — each is a possible direct path between two sites that could be constructed.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The predetermined number of excavation sites the director must select and interconnect with access tracks (the tree must span exactly this many sites).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one excavation site at one end of a candidate access track (one endpoint of the potential path).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other excavation site at the opposite end of the candidate access track (the other endpoint).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length or construction cost of the candidate access track between the two sites u and v; used to sum total path construction length when selecting the connected, loop-free network.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of bike docking stations shown on the map (the total count of graph nodes).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible bike-lane segments between stations on the map (the total count of graph edges available to build).

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of stations the planner must choose so that they form one connected, acyclic network (the target size of the tree).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of one endpoint station for this candidate bike-lane segment.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of the other endpoint station for this candidate bike-lane segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the bike-lane segment between the two stations; summing lengths of chosen links gives the total lane length to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vineyard parcels available on the map (the number of nodes in the full graph). This is the pool of parcels you may choose from when selecting exactly k parcels to connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential pipe connections listed between parcels (the number of edges in the input). Each entry corresponds to a candidate pipe that could be installed to link two parcels.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of vineyard parcels that must be chosen and interconnected into a single irrigation network. The final plan must include exactly this many parcels, be connected, and contain no closed loops.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID) of one endpoint parcel for this candidate pipe segment. Together with parcel_v it defines which two parcels that pipe would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID) of the other endpoint parcel for this candidate pipe segment. Combined with parcel_u it forms the pair of parcels that this pipe would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The weight for this candidate pipe segment: its physical pipe length and/or installation cost. These weights are summed over chosen segments and the solver seeks the set of pipes that connects exactly k parcels with minimum total of these values.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of sensor nodes available in the deployment (the count of distinct sensors that may be selected).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of provided pairwise radio link entries (each entry is a possible direct connection between two sensors, regardless of whether it will be used).

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of sensors that must be chosen and connected into a single loop-free network (the tree must span exactly this many sensors).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint sensor for this potential radio link (one of the two sensor nodes this link would connect).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint sensor for this potential radio link (the second sensor node this link would connect).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The distance (or cost) of the direct radio link between the two sensors u and v; these distances are summed for any chosen links and are the values minimized when building the k-node tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of wells on the village map. Each node represents a single well that could be included in the supply network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential direct pipe connections listed between wells. Each edge corresponds to a candidate straight pipe that can be built between two wells.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of wells that must be included in the final pipeline network (the tree). It is mandatory that exactly this many wells are connected, forming a single connected acyclic supply line.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one endpoint well for this potential pipe segment. Together with 'v' it defines which two wells the segment would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other endpoint well for this potential pipe segment. The pair (well_u_id, well_v_id) denotes the two wells connected by this candidate pipe.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (distance) of the pipe required to directly connect the two wells specified by well_u_id and well_v_id. The solver sums these lengths for chosen segments and seeks the set that yields the minimum total length while connecting exactly wells_to_connect wells without cycles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct buildings/sites shown on the campus map (i.e., the number of graph nodes available to choose from).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential fiber links listed between buildings on the map (i.e., the number of graph edges described). Each represents a candidate cable run you could install.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of buildings you must select and connect. Your final design must span exactly this many buildings and form a single loop-free network (a tree).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier/name of one endpoint building for this potential fiber link (one node of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier/name of the other endpoint building for this potential fiber link (the other node of the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost of using this link, expressed as the physical fiber length (or equivalent cost) between the two buildings; this value is summed when that edge is included in the chosen tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of utility poles shown on the city map. Each pole is a distinct node you may choose to include; identifiers for poles in edge entries refer to this set.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible direct cable runs between pairs of poles on the map. Each of these corresponds to one potential connection you can use and will be listed with its two endpoints and its length.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of poles you must select and connect into a tree. You must choose exactly this many poles (no duplicates), connect them so every chosen pole is reachable from every other, and avoid any closed loops; the chosen tree should minimize total cable length.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint pole for this potential cable segment. Matches one of the poles among total_poles.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint pole for this potential cable segment. Together with pole_u_id, it defines which two poles the cable would connect (undirected).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of installing cable along this segment between pole_u_id and pole_v_id. The planner sums chosen segments' lengths to compute the total cable used; the goal is to minimize this total while spanning exactly poles_to_connect poles without cycles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of ranger posts (nodes) available in the park that can potentially be opened; posts are assumed to be identified by indices from 1..num_nodes and used as endpoints of trails.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential trails (edges) provided in the instance, each describing a buildable connection between two posts with a known distance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of ranger posts that must be opened and connected into a single, loop-free network (a tree). The chosen solution must include exactly this many posts.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint post identifier for this potential trail; refers to one of the ranger posts (an integer matching the post index space).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint post identifier for this potential trail; paired with post_u to describe an undirected candidate trail between two posts.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The distance (cost) to build the trail between post_u and post_v. This nonnegative numeric value is what will be summed for all chosen trails and must be minimized subject to selecting exactly target_open_posts in a connected, acyclic network.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vendor stalls in the market diagram (each stall is a node that could be chosen to receive utilities).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible cable segments shown in the diagram (each represents a potential connector between two stalls, with an associated cost).

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of stalls the organizers must choose to connect with utilities (the tree must span exactly this many stalls).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint stall for this possible cable segment (one end of the connector).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint stall for this possible cable segment (the other end of the connector).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost to lay the cable for this segment between the two specified stalls; these costs are summed for all chosen segments in the final wiring plan.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of observation hides available in the reserve — i.e., the number of nodes in the graph representing all possible hide locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate footpaths between hides — i.e., the number of edges given; each entry is a possible path that could be built or used to connect hides.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of hides the trust must choose so that the selected hides are connected into a single tree (no cycles); the solution must span exactly this many hides.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint hide of a candidate footpath; refers to the identifier for a specific observation hide (one node of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint hide of the candidate footpath; refers to the identifier for the second observation hide connected by this edge.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length or cost of the footpath between hide_u and hide_v (e.g., meters or construction/walking cost). When this path is included in the chosen tree its length contributes to the total sum to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of access points (e.g., manholes or service nodes) in the town's sewer network that are considered as candidate nodes to include. These are the node identifiers from which the team may choose exactly k to connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate pipe segments (possible direct connections) between access points. Each corresponds to a measured/estimated pipe installation option with a known length between two access points.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of access points the sewer team must select and connect into one acyclic system. The chosen layout must span exactly this many nodes and be connected without loops.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint access point (node) for this candidate pipe segment. Matches one of the node labels from the set of total access points.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint access point (node) for this candidate pipe segment. Together with access_point_u defines which two access points the segment would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The installation length (cost) of the pipe segment connecting access_point_u and access_point_v. This length is the value summed when evaluating total pipe installed and is the quantity minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential sensor installation locations (graph nodes). These are the numbered sites from which you may select exactly k to connect into the network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate communication links (graph edges) available between sensor sites. Each corresponds to a possible physical connection you may choose to install, with an associated cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The predetermined number of sensor sites that must be included in the final network. The chosen links must connect exactly this many sites into one connected, cycle-free topology.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index) of one endpoint sensor site for this candidate link. Together with site_v_id it specifies which two sites this possible link would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index) of the other endpoint sensor site for this candidate link. The link is undirected; (site_u_id, site_v_id) denotes the pair of sites it would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Installation cost (edge weight) of the candidate link between site_u_id and site_v_id. The objective is to minimize the sum of link_cost values for the selected links forming the k-node, connected, cycle-free network.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of stations shown on the map (all available station nodes). This integer tells the solver how many distinct station identifiers exist in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible track segments (candidate links) between stations provided on the map. Each corresponds to a potential undirected connection the consultant may choose to build.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of stations that must be included in the final plan. The consultant must pick exactly this many stations and connect them into a single loop-free network (a tree) of minimum total new track length.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint station of a candidate track segment. Used together with 'v' to denote which two stations that potential segment would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint station of a candidate track segment. The pair (u, v) denotes an undirected possible link between two stations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of the candidate track segment connecting stations u and v. The consultant sums the lengths of chosen segments (counting each chosen segment once) and aims to minimize this total while connecting exactly 'stations_to_connect' stations without cycles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential lookout sites (nodes) on the mountain map. The solver treats these as the available watchpoints from which exactly k must be selected.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate straight access paths (edges) between watchpoints listed for the map. Each corresponds to a possible direct connection that can be built between two watchpoints.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of lookout points the rescue chief must choose. The chosen watchpoints must form a connected, loop-free network (a tree) and the selection must include exactly this many nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one endpoint watchpoint for this candidate path. Paired with 'v' to name the two watchpoints the path would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other endpoint watchpoint for this candidate path.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (or cost) of the direct path between watchpoint_u and watchpoint_v. If this path is included in the final plan it adds this amount to the total distance to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of barns on the farm (the number of vertices). This is the full set of barns you may choose from when selecting exactly k barns to enclose.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available fence sections in stock (the number of edges). Each fence piece represents a possible connection between two barns that can be used to join them.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of barns the farmer must select and connect into a single joined enclosure (the tree must span exactly this many barns).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one endpoint barn for a given fence piece. Used together with 'barn_v' to specify which two barns that fence could join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other endpoint barn for the fence piece; pairs with 'barn_u' to define the two barns this piece would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (or cost) of the fence piece that connects barn_u and barn_v, typically a positive number (e.g., meters). The goal is to minimize the sum of chosen fence_length values while forming a cycle-free connected enclosure of exactly k barns.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate relay towers (sites) available for the job. These are the graph nodes from which the crew must choose exactly k towers to include in the final built tree.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate microwave links between candidate towers. Each represents a possible undirected connection the crew could build, with an associated construction cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of towers the crew must select (k). The chosen towers must be connected by selected links into a single acyclic network (tree) spanning exactly this many sites.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index or ID) of one endpoint tower for this candidate microwave link. Refers to a specific candidate tower from the pool of sites.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index or ID) of the other endpoint tower for this candidate microwave link. Together with 'endpoint_u_site' it defines which two towers the link would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (weight) to build the microwave connection between the two endpoint towers. The objective is to minimize the sum of costs of the selected links that connect the chosen k towers into a tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of exhibits (nodes) on the museum map — the full set of exhibits the curator can choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of permitted corridors (edges) drawn on the map; each corridor is a possible passageway between two exhibits.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of exhibits the curator must pick so that the chosen exhibits are connected by selected corridors without forming any circular passageways.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint exhibit of a specific permitted corridor; together with 'v' it names which two exhibits the corridor could link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint exhibit of the corridor; pairs with 'u' to specify the two exhibits connected by this corridor.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the corridor between exhibits u and v; adding this value contributes to the total corridor length the curator is trying to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of houses (graph nodes) in the neighborhood that are candidates for wiring; each is a potential home the electrician may choose to include in the k-home network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct available line segments (graph edges) that can be installed between pairs of houses; each segment has an associated installation cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of houses the electrician must select and interconnect into one connected, loop-free network (a tree). The solution must include exactly this many houses.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint house of a candidate line segment, given by its node identifier; represents one home that the segment could connect to another home.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint house of the same candidate line segment, given by its node identifier; together with 'house_endpoint_u' it defines which two homes the segment links.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to install that specific line segment between the two endpoint houses; when chosen, this cost contributes to the total installation cost that must be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations in the region that could host an aid station (each location corresponds to a graph node).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate roads connecting pairs of locations (each road corresponds to a graph edge that can be chosen to link aid stations).

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of locations that must be selected as aid stations; the chosen roads must connect exactly this many stations into a tree.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this road (one of the two locations that this road connects).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this road (the second location that this road connects).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Travel time (weight) required to traverse this road between the two endpoint locations; used to compute the total travel time of the selected connecting roads.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of local leaders in the community pool you may choose from (the number of people represented as nodes in the graph).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible pairwise introductions recorded between leaders (the number of edges in the graph). Each represents a possible arranged introduction with a known effort.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of leaders you must select to form the leadership circle. You must pick exactly this many people and connect them via introductions.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a possible introduction: the identifier of the first leader involved in this potential introduction (one node of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a possible introduction: the identifier of the second leader involved in this potential introduction (the other node of the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The effort score required to arrange this specific introduction between leader_u and leader_v. These efforts are added for the chosen introductions and should be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of decorative ponds available on the site (the graph's nodes). This is the universe of ponds you may choose from when selecting exactly k ponds to connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available piping segments that can be laid between ponds (the graph's edges). Each segment connects two specific ponds and has a given length; these are the candidate connections for forming the water network.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of ponds you must choose to include in the water system. Your final layout must connect exactly this many ponds into one connected, loop-free network (a tree).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint pond of this piping segment (identified by its node index or label). Together with 'v' this indicates which two ponds the segment can join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint pond of this piping segment (identified by its node index or label). The segment connects the ponds named by 'u' and 'v'.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length of this piping segment (the edge weight). When selecting segments to connect the chosen ponds, you sum these lengths and aim to minimize the total while keeping the network connected and cycle-free.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of landing pads shown on the full map — the pool of available pads you may choose from for the k-pad connected system.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of permitted aerial corridors on the map between pads — each represents a potential corridor you can assign between two pads.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of landing pads you must choose so the selected pads form one connected system (tree) with no cyclic flight loops; the plan must span this many pads.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (node label) of one endpoint landing pad for a specific aerial corridor in the map.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (node label) of the other endpoint landing pad for the same aerial corridor.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (distance) of the aerial corridor between pad_u and pad_v; this value is the cost added to the plan when that corridor is assigned and is summed across chosen corridors to evaluate total plan cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of campus buildings under consideration (graph nodes). Each building is a distinct node id that can be chosen for conduit connection.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available conduit routes between buildings (graph edges). Each route represents a possible conduit run you may use to connect selected buildings.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of buildings you must select and interconnect with new conduit. The resulting selected buildings must form a single connected tree with no cycles and contain exactly this many nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint building id for a specific available route. Together with 'v' this identifies which two buildings that route would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint building id for the route. The pair (u, v) denotes an available conduit path between those two buildings.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length or cost of the conduit along the route between u and v (e.g., meters or cost units). These weights are summed for the selected tree and should be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of film sets available on the lot (each corresponds to a graph node). This is the count of distinct sets you may choose from when selecting exactly k active sets.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of approved backstage walkway segments (each corresponds to a graph edge) that may be installed between sets. Only these segments can be used to connect the chosen sets.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of film sets the coordinator must activate and connect. The final installed walkways must produce a connected, acyclic layout spanning exactly this many sets.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an approved walkway segment: the identifier of the first film set that this segment can connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the approved walkway segment: the identifier of the second film set that this segment can connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost to install this approved walkway segment between the two endpoint sets. The coordinator sums chosen segments' costs; the goal is to minimize that total while connecting the selected k sets without cycles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential supplier locations shown on the map (graph vertices). Each is a candidate stop the coordinator may choose as part of the k selected supply points.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate roads connecting supplier locations (graph edges). Each road is a possible delivery route between two locations and has an associated distance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: Exact number of supplier locations the coordinator must select and connect into a single, loop-free delivery network (the tree must span exactly this many locations).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one endpoint supplier location for this candidate road. Used together with 'v' to specify which two locations the road connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other endpoint supplier location for this candidate road; pairs with 'u' to define the road between two locations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Distance (route length) of the candidate road between the two endpoints u and v. When a road is included in the chosen delivery network its distance contributes to the total route length to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct server hub locations shown on the floor plan (i.e., the number of nodes in the graph). Use this to know how many hub labels exist and to validate node identifiers in the fiber options.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate fiber runs listed on the plan (i.e., the number of edges in the graph). Each represents a possible cable between two hubs that can be installed at the listed cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of server hubs you must choose and interconnect into a single, loop-free network (the tree must span exactly this many hubs). This is the k in the k-MST requirement.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label) of one endpoint hub for this candidate fiber run. Matches one of the hub labels from total_server_hubs_available.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label) of the other endpoint hub for this candidate fiber run. Together with hub_endpoint_a it defines which two hubs this cable would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to install this particular fiber run between the two specified hubs. Solver sums selected fiber_install_cost values to compute the total installation expense for the chosen k-hub tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vendor stalls available in the festival area (the graph's nodes). Each stall is a candidate to be included in the powered setup.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of approved trunk line segments measured between stalls (the graph's edges). Each segment represents a possible piece of wiring that can be chosen to link stalls.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of vendor stalls that must be selected and connected by trunk lines. The final wiring layout must span exactly this many stalls, be connected, and contain no loops.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one vendor stall at one end of this trunk segment. Used with 'v' to indicate which two stalls this segment would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other vendor stall at the opposite end of this trunk segment. Together with 'u' this defines the undirected connection between two stalls.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (or cost) of this trunk segment — the amount of wiring required (e.g., in meters). The solver sums these values for chosen segments and seeks the minimum total length while connecting exactly k stalls without cycles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available sensor sites (vertices) in the survey area. Use this to understand how many candidate locations there are to choose from when selecting exactly k sites to form the survey route.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential tracks (undirected connections) between pairs of sites. Each candidate track is a possible open route segment the crew could use; the solver will consider these when building a connected, loop-free route spanning k sites.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The required number of distinct sensor sites to include in the final route. You must choose exactly this many sites so that they form one connected acyclic survey route (a tree) with minimum total travel distance.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint site identifier for a candidate track. Interpreted as a specific sensor site (by index or label) that can be connected to site_b by opening this track.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint site identifier for the same candidate track. Together with site_a it specifies which two sensor sites would be connected if this track is opened.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance (weight/cost) of the track between site_a and site_b. When selecting tracks to form the connected, loop-free survey route over exactly k sites, the solver minimizes the sum of these distances.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations in the city's road network (each node represents a candidate community center site or road junction among which centers may be chosen).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available road segments that directly connect pairs of locations in the network (each edge is a potential street segment you can include in the plan).

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of community centers the plan must serve — i.e., the number of locations that must be selected and connected into a single loop-free route (tree).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location for this specific road segment (one of the two locations the street connects).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location for this road segment (the second location that the street connects).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length or travel distance of this road segment connecting the two endpoints; this value is the cost added to the plan if the segment is selected and is used when minimizing the total distance of the chosen tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distribution hubs in the network pool from which you may choose; every hub is a candidate location identified by an index or ID.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential direct transfer lanes listed between pairs of hubs; each entry represents a possible lane you can open (one-way or two-way) with a specified distance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of hubs you must select to include in the final loop-free connected plan (the tree must span exactly this many hubs).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or ID) of one endpoint hub of this candidate transfer lane; together with 'hub_endpoint_v' it defines which two hubs the lane would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or ID) of the other endpoint hub of this candidate transfer lane; paired with 'hub_endpoint_u' to locate the lane between two hubs.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The distance (or cost) of opening this transfer lane between the two hubs; these distances are summed for the chosen lanes and should be minimized while forming an acyclic connected network over exactly 'target_hub_count' hubs.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of individual street light fixtures available in the neighborhood layout (every node represents one fixture that could be wired).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct possible conduit runs (candidate cable paths) between fixtures; each corresponds to an available connection option between two fixtures.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of fixtures the crew must include in the single, connected, loop-free circuit (the tree must span exactly this many fixtures).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint fixture identifier for a particular available conduit run (the first light pole served by this conduit option).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint fixture identifier for the same conduit run (the second light pole served by this conduit option).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (weight) to install that conduit run between the two fixtures — representing materials/labor — used to evaluate total plan cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential pump-station locations (graph vertices) available in the pipeline planning area.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible pipe segments (graph edges) that could be built between candidate sites.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of pump stations the design must include; the chosen stations must be connected into one cycle-free network spanning this many sites.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint site identifier for a candidate pipe segment — a specific potential pump-station location.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint site identifier for the candidate pipe segment, indicating the two sites this segment would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of that candidate pipe segment; used to sum total built pipe length when selecting segments for the k‑station tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate filming sites on the location map. This is the number of distinct site IDs you may choose from when selecting exactly k sites to include in the service-road layout.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential direct service roads shown on the map between candidate sites. Each entry represents a possible road you could build between two sites, with an associated mileage cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of filming sites you must pick for the shoot. The chosen sites must be connected by built service roads into a single acyclic layout (a tree) and you cannot pick more or fewer than this number.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint site for this potential service road. Together with 'site_endpoint_v' this names the two candidate filming sites that could be connected by building this road.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint site for this potential service road. Combined with 'site_endpoint_u', it specifies which two candidate sites the road would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The mileage (length) of the potential service road between the two endpoint sites. When you include this road in the final layout you add this value to the total road miles to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighborhood junctions available in the city map (all numbered uniquely). This is the count of nodes from which you may select exactly k to wire.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of potential coaxial link segments given in the dataset. Each described link connects two of the junctions and has a specified physical length.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of junctions you must choose to include in the design. The final coax layout must connect exactly this many junctions into a single loop-free network (a tree).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one endpoint junction for this potential coax link. Refer to one of the total_junctions.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other endpoint junction for this potential coax link. Together with junction_a_id it defines which two junctions the link would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The physical length (or cost) of that coaxial link between the two listed junctions. When selecting the k-junction tree, sum of these lengths for chosen links is what you minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of raised beds in the garden layout (the number of nodes in the graph). Use this to enumerate bed IDs and to verify that the required number to connect does not exceed available beds.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate hose segments between beds (the number of edges in the graph). Each item represents a potential hose you could lay between two specific beds.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of raised beds that must be included in the single connected, loop-free watering network. The solution must span exactly this many beds while minimizing total hose length.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (ID or index) of one raised bed at one end of this candidate hose segment. References a specific bed among the total_raised_beds.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (ID or index) of the other raised bed at the opposite end of this candidate hose segment. Together with bed_endpoint_u describes which two beds this hose would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the hose needed to connect the two beds specified by bed_endpoint_u and bed_endpoint_v. The solver will sum these lengths for chosen segments and aim to minimize that total; units match the garden layout (e.g., meters).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct field plots available in the survey area. All plot identifiers referenced in the instance refer to these plots.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential survey links (pairwise connections) provided between plots in the instance.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of plots that must be chosen and connected by the measurement tree; the final chosen structure must span exactly this many plots.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint plot of a potential survey link (one end of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint plot of the potential survey link (the other end of the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length or distance of the survey link connecting plot_u and plot_v; this numeric cost contributes to the total link distance to be minimized for the k-plot measurement tree.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of small-cell sites (graph nodes) available in the network layout; the solver treats this as the full set of candidate sites indexed in the edge list.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of possible backhaul links (graph edges) listed below; each item describes a candidate direct connection between two small cells with an associated cost.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of small cells the operator must activate and connect. The chosen activated sites must form a connected, acyclic layout (a tree) spanning exactly this many nodes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint small-cell site for this candidate backhaul link; matches a node index in the network.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint small-cell site for this candidate backhaul link; together with cell_u_id defines the link's endpoints.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost (weight) to establish the backhaul link between the two specified small cells; the solver sums these for chosen links and minimizes total cost subject to selecting a tree over exactly k nodes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct transformer locations (potential sites) available in the utility network instance. These are the nodes the planner may choose from when activating exactly k sites.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available power line segments (distinct candidate connections) between transformer sites in the instance. Each segment connects two site IDs and may be purchased and laid if chosen.

global_fields.name: k
global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of transformer sites the planner must activate and interconnect into one connected, acyclic layout. The chosen plan must select exactly this many sites and connect them with selected segments.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint transformer site for this power line segment. Matches a site index from the instance's list of transformer locations.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint transformer site for this power line segment. Together with site_u_id it defines which two sites the segment would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (or cost proportional to length) of this power line segment between the two endpoint sites. Use this value to sum the total length of chosen segments; the plan with the smallest total wins. Units are as given in the instance (e.g., meters or kilometers).
